Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Income of the claimant’s partner

85016 In a claim for SPC, calculate income of the claimant’s partner in the same way as for the claimant 1.

The income should then be treated as the claimant’s income 2.


Note: In SPC a member of a couple is referred to as a partner and both members are referred to as

partners3. DMG 77117.6 gives guidance that a person subject to immigration control should be treated
as not being a member of the same household. The income of a partner subject to immigration control
should not be treated as the claimant's income.


                                               1 SPC Regs, reg 14; 2 SPC Act 02, s 5; 3 SPC Regs, reg 1(3)

1. are in GB and


2. have reached the qualifying age and


3. satisfy the conditions to get a GC or SC and


4. are not a member of a


      4.1 couple where the other member is entitled to SPC or


      4.2 mixed-age couple (see DMG 77035 and 77140)


      4.3 polygamous marriage (see DMG 77016) where the other party to the marriage or the additional
      spouse are members of the same household and entitled to SPC (but see DMG 77140 et seq) and


5. have made a valid claim2 and


6. where relevant, their partner, satisfy the NI provisions (see DMG Chapter 02) 3.


           1 SPC Act 02, s 1(2) & 4(1) & (1A); SPC Regs, Sch III, para 1(3); 2 SS A Act 92, s 1(1) & (4); 3 s 1(1A)

The captured DMG 78077 categories are: a person aged under 18; a person receiving source-defined “AA”, highest- or middle-rate DLA care, standard- or enhanced-rate PIP or ADP daily living, or AFIP; a person certified as blind or severely sight impaired by a consultant ophthalmologist or treated as such; a person living with the claimant to care for the claimant or partner who is engaged by a charitable or voluntary organisation which charges the claimant or partner for their services; that carer’s partner; and a source-defined qualifying young person, or a child for Child Benefit purposes. DMG 78008 limits treated blindness to 28 weeks after regained eyesight and no longer being certified. A voluntary organisation is non-profit and is not a public authority or local authority. Named young-person definitions have age, education, training, benefit-receipt and interruption conditions; neither education alone nor being under 20 is enough. DMG 78078(1) requires first joining the household to care for the claimant or partner, with the claimant or partner satisfying the additional-amount conditions immediately beforehand, and applies only for the first 12 weeks after joining. Its commercial-payment route concerns a person who is not a close relative: payment liability runs either from that person to the claimant or partner for occupation of their dwelling, or from the claimant or partner to that person for occupation of that person’s dwelling; it also covers membership of that person’s household. DMG 78079 requires legal liability and a payment broadly comparable to a lodger’s similar accommodation and facilities. The joint-occupation route requires co-ownership or joint liability to the same landlord, with its non-close-relative condition and the person’s-partner branch. The close-relative exception requires satisfying DMG 78078(3) or (4) as well as the timing condition: the claimant or partner’s co-ownership or joint liability must have arisen before 11 April 1988 or, if later, on or before first occupation; the note uses the right-to-occupy date, not a later moving-in date. Close relative has the captured legal, adoptive and half-sibling meanings. DMG 78080’s registered shared-lives route must retain the accommodation/support and commercial licence conditions and the exclusion where other people cannot be ignored; its completed example is not a general award rule or a current rate. Memo 02/25 paragraph 15 adds Pension Age Disability Payment to the ignored-person benefit list from 21 October 2024, separately from the memo’s claimant/partner and housing-deduction propositions. The dated statutory paragraph 2 also contains Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance wording requiring separate legal reconciliation; this concept does not consolidate it. Receipt conditions need the full DMG 78060 continuation: its partner-patient item must not be transferred automatically to a third person. Residence, receipt and component, age, care arrangements, relationship, liability and relevant dates remain unknown until evidenced. Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"Source-bounded navigation through DMG 78065–78076, separate from ignoring a person’s presence under 78077–78080 and from deciding whether partners remain one household. Normal residence is where a person usually lives: exceptional visits or absences are disregarded, and temporary absence does not itself change the normal home. DMG 78067 requires factual consideration of time, frequency, permanence, intentions, circumstances, degree of sharing, services, other accommodation and liabilities. An address, university term or overnight stay alone does not settle that assessment. Sharing only a bathroom, lavatory or communal area, or separate legal payment liabilities to the same landlord, has the captured sharing exceptions. Kitchen sharing can exist without entering or using it when personal items are stored or meals prepared there; merely passing through to a self-contained flat is different. DMG 78072–78075 require the contractual capacity and intention to create legal relations, an obligation for occupation from a recognised source of law, and the stipulated connection between non-payment and ending the licence or lease; another liability to a third party is not the same-landlord condition. Retain the England-and-Wales scope and presumption in the captured capacity passage rather than infer incapacity from a diagnosis. For an overnight carer, establish the separate address, actual use and frequency, postal address and Council Tax registration. All residence and contractual facts remain unknown until evidenced.
